article.title: DuckDB 1.5.6 Ships Correctness and Crash Fixes, and Previews a Windows Build of v2.0 That Ran TPC-H More Than 6x Faster
article.summary: DuckDB's sixth 1.5 patch release fixes wrong-result and crash bugs; the team also reports a v2.0.0-dev Windows build finishing a TPC-H SF300 run in 129 seconds versus 822.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

The DuckDB team released version 1.5.6 on September 28, 2026. According to the [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html), it is the sixth patch release in the 1.5 (Variegata) line and ships bugfixes, performance improvements and security patches. The same post gives an early Windows benchmark of the upcoming v2.0.0-dev, which the team says was more than 6x faster than v1.5.6 on a TPC-H workload.

## What Is in 1.5.6

The [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html) groups its highlighted fixes into correctness, crashes and internal errors, generic bugfixes, and miscellaneous changes.

**Correctness.** Fixes listed by the team include LIMIT pushdown through a volatile projection with an OFFSET, filters no longer being pushed through aggregates on volatile groups, UNNEST pushdown, and NULL handling in Top-N window elimination. Other items cover wrong results from common subplan elimination with UNION ALL arms that share a join subtree, silent truncation of very long integer literals into HUGEINT, and `max` on a Hive partition column after file pruning. The post also lists fixes for TIME_NS values in Parquet and for Parquet VARIANT shredding.

**Crashes and internal errors.** The [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html) lists a crash in Top-N with LIMIT 0, a segfault in `url_decode` with `TRY()` on dictionary-encoded columns, a failed checkpoint marker recovery, and a change to close the main write-ahead-log handle before renaming over it during WAL recovery. The [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/tag/v1.5.6) carry the crash and WAL entries as well.

**Other changes.** Per the blog post, the release adds an `enable_optimistic_write` setting, hardens temporary file reads, always quotes identifiers in error messages, and unifies C API symbol versioning for clients and extensions while stabilizing all v1 APIs. The [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/tag/v1.5.6) also list a backport of DuckDB 2.0 API spellings to 1.5 and version bumps for extensions including DuckLake and iceberg.

## Windows Preview of v2.0

Under the heading "Looking Ahead: DuckDB v2.0 on Windows," the [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html) describes a test on Windows 11 25H2 on a laptop with 128 GB RAM and 12 AMD Ryzen AI 300 CPU cores with simultaneous multithreading, yielding 24 threads. The team used the TPC-H SF300 dataset and ran each query twice on both DuckDB v1.5.6 and v2.0.0-dev (alpha43586).

The post reports that the total runtime for v1.5.6 was 822 seconds, while for v2.0.0-dev it was 129 seconds. The team writes: "That's more than 6× faster!" It attributes the improvement to several optimizations, including a switch to the clang-cl compiler and a new allocator.

The team also cautions readers: "please do not expect a 6× speedup to generalize to all workloads". It adds that users should still see significant improvements. The result is a single vendor-run benchmark on one laptop configuration, and no independent replication appears in the sources reviewed.

## What We Don't Know

- How the Windows gains divide between the compiler switch and the new allocator; the post names both without separating them.
- How v2.0.0-dev performs on Linux or macOS relative to 1.5.6; the post's comparison covers Windows only.
- The final v2.0.0 feature set beyond what the post says. The team says v2.0.0 is due in October.

## Context

The v2.0 line was previously covered by The Machine Herald, which [reported in August](/article/2026-08/20-duckdb-previews-v20-cyanoptera-replacing-its-postgres-derived-parser-with-a-peg-grammar-ahead-of-a-fall-release) on the project's preview of v2.0 and its parser replacement.
